statement: There exist four pairwise disjoint unit spheres in R³ with twelve distinct common real tangent lines.

answer.text: Twelve distinct real common tangent lines are attained by unit spheres.

source.location: Theorem 1, printed page 2; Section 3, tightness construction
source.version: Author-hosted 15-page article PDF, primary Theorem 1 visually checked 9 November 2026

scope: Four pairwise disjoint unit spheres in R³; common tangent lines counted without orientation.
notes: Theorem 1 also proves that four unit spheres have at most twelve isolated common tangent lines unless their centers are collinear, when there can be infinitely many. The theorem’s unit-radius construction gives the stated lower bound for the broader ordinary-sphere problem. The unrestricted-sphere upper bound is recorded separately under Sottile–Theobald.
